structure.note: Class A shares carry one vote and Class B shares twenty votes; Class H (held by Airbnb's own subsidiary) has none. Brian Chesky holds 31.9% of the voting power, Nathan Blecharczyk 31.1% and Joseph Gebbia 17.6% (2026 proxy). The founders are parties to a voting agreement under which they vote for each other's election to the board. No single holder has a majority.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001559720-26-000004, filed February 12, 2026; its tables list years oldest first, 2023, 2024, 2025) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-175062, ownership as of April 8, 2026). OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives Chesky 1.0% of Class A, 35.6% of Class B and 31.9% of voting power but no percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and the 11.22% economic share is in leader.derived. Excluding Class H is a judgment call, explained in derived.method; including it gives 11.05%. Footnote (1) lists his holdings across his own name and several trusts, including 15,000,000 Class B shares in two 2026 grantor retained annuity trusts; he has no voting or dispositive power over the shares in three of the family trusts listed. 5% HOLDERS: the proxy states holder percentages only by class, so they are recorded on a class basis: The Vanguard Group 9.1% of Class A (1.0% of voting power, Schedule 13G/A of October 30, 2025) and Sequoia Capital entities 9.9% of Class B (plus 510,666 Class A, marked *; 8.8% of voting power, Schedule 13G of November 5, 2024). The proxy also lists the Airbnb Host Endowment LLC (all 9,200,000 non-voting Class H shares, a wholly-owned subsidiary) and the co-founders Blecharczyk (61,115,962 Class B, 34.8%) and Gebbia (34,569,980 Class B, 19.7%) in the directors' table. No dividends have been paid, and the cash-flow statement has no dividend line. Buybacks exclude $561 million of taxes paid on equity awards.

ecosystem.notes: GBV includes host earnings, service fees, cleaning fees and taxes. It is recorded when a booking is made, while revenue is recognized at check-in, so the two are timed differently. From FY2025 the 10-K pairs GBV with 'Nights and Seats Booked' (formerly 'Nights and Experiences Booked'). The 10-K does not state total host earnings, so payouts is null.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet, net of refunds, from the ASU 2023-09 table by jurisdiction (federal 65, state 46, foreign 121). R&D not reported as a separate line. Airbnb reports 'Product development' ($2,354 million in 2025; tagged us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense in XBRL), which the 10-K describes as costs of developing the platform without calling it research and development, so it is not recorded.

footprint.notes: usStates: two rows per state (50 states and DC), both from Airbnb-authored Flourish maps embedded in Airbnb newsroom posts; the rows sit in each chart's data <script> block. (1) The 2025 U.S. economic impact map (news.airbnb.com/hosts-and-guests-boost-us-economy-by-a-record-93b-in-2025, Apr 15, 2026): jobs supported, GDP and total tax revenue by state, internal IMPLAN estimates, replacing the 2024 map. (2) The 2025 tourism-tax map (news.airbnb.com/hosts-and-guests-generated-17-3b-in-tourism-taxes-for-communities-around-the-world, Apr 6, 2026): taxes Airbnb collected and remitted on behalf of hosts, now for every state, replacing the 2024 newsroom list of 19 states and DC. State sums fall short of the national headlines (jobs about 1.07 million vs 'more than 1.1 million'; GDP about $91.9 billion vs 'more than $93 billion in economic activity'; tax about $23.8 billion vs 'over $26 billion'); tourism taxes sum to $2,710.6 million vs 'approximately $2.7 billion'. Countries: jobs supported in 9 Asia-Pacific countries from Airbnb's Oxford Economics-commissioned 2024 study (company-commissioned); the country pages were re-read on 2026-11-24 and still report 2024, so no newer edition was found. Thailand is 'Nearly 110,000', recorded as 110,000. Vietnam's page is not part of that study: it reports 2025 from Airbnb's internal IMPLAN analysis ('supported more than 85,000 jobs'), and is now added under the same internal-analysis metric as Canada. Canada's 'more than 100,000 estimated jobs nationwide in 2025' (plus) is from Airbnb's internal IMPLAN analysis in its 2025 Canada release (company-published), replacing the 2024 release's 'over 105,000'. Local-currency GDP figures per country were not recorded, to avoid mixing currencies. 10-K Item 2 names only the San Francisco headquarters.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001559720-26-000004). The cash-flow statement folds capex into "Other investing activities, net"; the 33 comes from the free-cash-flow reconciliation in MD&A. Income taxes paid now appear only as a 2025 total by jurisdiction under ASU 2023-09. Host payouts are not in revenue or operating cash flow (funds payable to hosts move in financing), so the money hosts earn is counted once, in salesEnabled. Interest income (0.705bn) is received inside operating cash flow but is not revenue, so it lowers paidOut.

pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end count from the FY2025 10-K; it excludes the approximately 13,000 third-party workers who handle most community support contacts. Payroll: the 10-K gives no total of salaries, benefits or personnel costs, so the 2026 proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used. Airbnb identified the median employee among all full-time, part-time and temporary employees at December 31, 2025, using annualized base salary and bonus target plus equity awarded in 2025. The CEO's 2025 total compensation ($242,122) was slightly above the median's.
